empty-mname.title: The SOA has no primary name server
empty-mname.detail: Fill in the host name of the name server holding the original copy of the zone.

invalid-mname.title: Invalid primary name server "{{mname}}"
invalid-mname.detail: The primary name server must be given as a valid host name, as defined by RFC 1035.

mname-is-cname.title: The primary name server "{{mname}}" is an alias
mname-is-cname.detail: A name server must be designated by a host name, never by a CNAME (RFC 2181 sec. 10.3).

empty-rname.title: The SOA has no contact address
empty-rname.detail: Fill in the mailbox of the person responsible for the zone, written as a domain name.

rname-has-at.title: The contact "{{rname}}" contains an "@"
rname-has-at.detail: In a SOA, the "@" of the address is replaced by a dot: write "{{suggestion}}" instead. Dots of the part before the "@" have to be escaped with a backslash.

invalid-rname.title: Invalid contact "{{rname}}"
invalid-rname.detail: The contact is an address written as a domain name: its first label is the part before the "@", the following ones must form a valid domain.

invalid-timer.title: Invalid duration "{{value}}"
invalid-timer.detail: The SOA timers are durations in seconds, between 0 and 4294967295.

refresh-too-short.title: The refresh time of {{refresh}} s is very short
refresh-too-short.detail: Secondary name servers check the zone for changes at this pace. RFC 1912 advises at least {{min}} seconds: below that, they mostly poll for nothing.

retry-not-below-refresh.title: The retry interval is not shorter than the refresh time
retry-not-below-refresh.detail: After a failed refresh, a secondary name server tries again after {{retry}} s, which should be quicker than its regular {{refresh}} s check.

expire-too-short.title: The zone expires after {{expire}} s only
expire-too-short.detail: A secondary name server failing a single refresh would stop answering for the zone before even retrying. The expiry should be much longer than the refresh and retry times added together, RFC 1912 suggests 2 to 4 weeks.

negative-ttl-too-long.title: Negative answers are cached for {{minttl}} s
negative-ttl-too-long.detail: Resolvers remember that a name does not exist for that long: a name created afterwards stays invisible to them in the meantime. RFC 2308 advises one to three hours, and no more than {{max}} seconds.
